title: Musk Confirms SpaceX-Nvidia 'Starmind AI1' Orbital Data Center Satellite Targeting Late 2027 Launch
detail: Elon Musk confirmed on August 24, 2026 that SpaceX and Nvidia have designed a space-optimized Vera Rubin NVL72 compute system for SpaceX's first orbital AI data center satellite, 'Starmind AI1,' targeting launch to orbit in Q4 2027 with 'significant scale' by 2028. Musk said SpaceX chose to use Nvidia GPUs exclusively because 'the Vera Rubin architecture is the best architecture,' and SpaceX envisions eventually deploying up to 1 million AI satellites functioning as a single distributed orbital data center — a buildout that would require the launch capacity SpaceX is pursuing with the planned $100B Starbase Louisiana spaceport announced the following day. The Q4 2027 target pulls forward the timeline SpaceX gave investors in its May 20, 2026 IPO S-1 filing, which described orbital data-center deployment as relying on 'unproven technologies, or technologies that do not exist' and targeted 2028 at the earliest — a gap analysts flagged given the unsolved engineering challenge of radiating hundreds of kilowatts of waste heat in the vacuum of space without ambient air or water cooling, something never accomplished at this scale.
